subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <scarter@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments follow-up

Hi Sam,

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC so we can lock scope and timelines:

Summary of ask: Atlas wants to validate Redwood for high-throughput payment-supporting prompts (token classification + entity extraction) and ensure production-grade latency and cost.

Proposed measurable success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 150 ms for 256-token context (service-level target)
- Throughput: sustained 2k requests/sec for inference pipeline (burst to 3k)
- Cost: inference cost <= $0.0005 per token (target average across workload)
- Quality: extraction F1 >= 92% on your labeled eval set; human reviewer pass-rate >= 95% on a 200-case sample

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline: 4 weeks total
- Week 0: MAA + access & onboarding (creds, test dataset, samples)
- Week 1: Integration + baseline runs (latency/throughput smoke tests)
- Week 2: Load testing & cost profiling (batching/quantization experiments)
- Week 3: Quality evals + human review; iterate on prompts/temperature
- Week 4: Final report + go/no-go decision; recommend next steps for Dedicated or private deployment

Owners: Jordan (AM) will own weekly check-ins and ops; Marissa (CS) will run onboarding and quality eval coordination; Atlas to own dataset labeling and access.

Next steps for you:
1) Confirm the success criteria above or propose edits
2) Share a test dataset sample (S3 link or Drive) and an internal contact for KMS/VPN needs
3) Confirm preferred kick-off window (we have availability next Tue or Wed)

Attached: redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf (high-level timeline) and evaluation-checklist.xlsx (template).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0192
From: Sam Carter <scarter@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <prao@atlas-payments.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments follow-up

Jordan,

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches our internal goals closely. A few points / minor edits:

- Latency: agree on p95 <= 150 ms for 256-token; we also want p99 documented during load tests (we don't need it as a hard pass/fail but should surface).
- Throughput: 2k sustained is correct. For the POC we'll target 1.5k in week 2 and ramp to 2k in week 3 if all goes well.
- Cost: target $0.0005/token is ambitious but acceptable as a POC benchmark — can you document how batching and KV caching will be measured?
- Quality: we'll provide a labeled eval set (5k rows) and a separate 200-case blind human review. F1 >= 92% is our goal.

Timeline: We prefer a May 10 kick-off (next Mon). Week 0 onboarding should include a short runbook for network/firewall whitelisting and KMS instructions.

Owners: I'll be the primary for Atlas. Priya (cc'd) is our SRE and will coordinate network/KMS.

We're good to proceed once you send the onboarding steps and confirm the May 10 slot.

— Sam
Sam Carter
Head of AI Engineering | Atlas Payments
scarter@atlas-payments.com | +1 617-555-0123

Date: 2027-05-03T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments follow-up

Sam — thanks, that works. Quick answers:

- p99: we will capture and share p50/p95/p99 histograms from the runtime during load tests.
- Batching/KV caching measurement: we'll run controlled experiments with and without prefix caching and with multiple batching profiles. Results will include tokens/sec, average cost/token, and per-request latency distribution.
- May 10 kickoff confirmed.

I've updated the attached plan with the May 10 kickoff and a short onboarding checklist (see redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf). Marissa will send the runbook for firewall/KMS by end of day tomorrow.

Action items I'm picking up:
- Send MAA + onboarding checklist (Jordan) — target 2027-05-04
- Schedule kick-off meeting for 2027-05-10 (Jordan/Marissa)
- Provide test dataset upload instructions (Marissa)

If that looks okay I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff and invite Priya + your engineering lead.

Hi Sam / Priya —

Looping in the CS runbook and a few practical notes for the kick-off:

- Firewall/KMS runbook: please open port 443 to our onboarding IPs and add our service account to the VPC peering allowlist if you're using private endpoints. I'll send a separate email with the exact IPs and the KMS key policy snippet.
- Test dataset: please upload a 5k-row CSV to the shared Drive link (or S3) and put a small sample (20 rows) in the onboarding folder so we can sanity-check quickly.
- Evaluation checklist: we'll run the following during week 2-3:
  * Baseline latency/throughput (no batching)
  * Batching profiles (batch sizes 1, 4, 16)
  * KV/prefix cache experiments (cold vs warm)
  * Cost modeling (tokens/sec, avg cost/token)
  * Quality evals (automated F1 + human review)

Deliverables by end of POC:
- Final metrics report (p50/p95/p99 latency histograms, throughput over time, avg cost/token)
- Quality report (F1, precision/recall, human pass-rate)
- Runbook for production rollout recommendations (batching/cache/quantization settings)

Next steps: I'll send the firewall/KMS snippet and schedule the May 10 kickoff for 30 minutes. Jordan — can you confirm which engineering leads we should invite?

Thanks — excited to get started.

— Marissa
